comments.author: Nicole Cruz
comments.comment: Most teams over-index on model choice. Your point about lower-level models + great context is spot on—what was the biggest surprise when you switched from a top-tier to a lower-cost model for a core agent task?

comments.author: Ramy A.
comments.comment:
Most agent benchmarks test reasoning, not the harness's ability to enforce guardrails. That's the real gap for production.

In my work, a robust harness can improve task success by 30%+ on the same model, purely by managing state and constraints better. The trick is defining those system-level rules before you even pick the orchestrator.

For those building business agents, what's your top priority in a harness: auditability, rule enforcement, or recovery from model deviations?

comments.author: SETU School
comments.comment: The missing piece is often sample size, not model choice. I ship evals where every agent metric gets a confidence interval and a p-value before it changes a model decision. How do you size eval sets for agentic tasks without blowing up cost? #LLMEvals #StatisticalSignificance #Agents

comments.author: Oliver Hassell
comments.comment:
Most agent harnesses fail on ownership, not model quality.

The routing layer has to decide which agent can write to the CRM, and the eval layer has to score the next action before it becomes memory.

I would track action precision and rollback rate before scaling personalization.

What guardrail would you add before letting agents touch account memory?

#AgenticAI
